about.ctaDescription: Join thousands of gamers who are tracking and sharing their gaming accomplishments with Steam Vault.

faq.answer1: Steam Vault is a platform that lets you view all of your achievements across Steam. We help you find your rarest achievements.
faq.answer2: Due to Steam's strict API guidelines, it is difficult to track achievement progress for many users, across thousands of games. Steam Vault aims to bridge that gap, while gathering as much data & insight as possible, and providing it to you (for free).
faq.answer3: Simply press the sign in button on the top right corner of the page. Connect your Steam account to start tracking your achievements.
faq.answer4: Steam Vault is completely free to use. There are no paid features. We are funded entirely by advertising and donations.
faq.answer5: Our data is updated systematically to maintain within Steam's API guidelines. If you feel like your data is not refreshing regularly, please reach out to us.
faq.answer6: Each user has a public profile page that can be shared via a unique URL. You can also generate shareable cards for individual achievements to post on social media.
faq.answer7: Achievement rarity is calculated based on a few factors. The "percentage" stat is from Steam directly, and it is unknown how that number is calculated. Our "score" represents how many people have unlocked the achievement. It is calculated using a rough estimate of how many people have played the game. We are always looking for new ways to analyze and visualize your achievements.

mission.paragraph1: Steam Vault was created with a simple goal: let gamers find their rarest achievements across the platform.
mission.paragraph2: Achievements aren't always just milestones; they can represent hours of dedication, learning, practicing, and grinding. For most people, no one else will ever notice this. Steam Vault aims to change that.
mission.paragraph3: Our platform is designed to celebrate your gaming journey, allowing you to view your achievements in a new light. We also aim to provide you with insights and other info to keep you going.

loadingScreen.description1: While developing Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare (2007), Infinity Ward studied real special forces training manuals, focusing on radio chatter, movement tactics, and body language, to craft a cinematic yet tactically grounded experience.
loadingScreen.description2: In Portal (2007), players are promised a literal cake, while being unknowingly lead to their demise. This tongue-in-cheek promise quickly evolved into an iconic reminder about empty incentives in game marketing.
loadingScreen.description3: Super Mario Bros. (1985) included a unused red "Koopa Troopa" enemy that had 2 lives. Leaked code for Super Mario All-Stars (1993) hints that this was planned as the default behavior for all Koopa Troopas.
loadingScreen.description4: GoldenEye 007 (1997) was the first game to feature a first-person shooter multiplayer mode on a console. It set the standard for FPS games on consoles, influencing countless titles that followed.
loadingScreen.description5: The original Legend of Zelda (1986) was one of the first console games to introduce a battery-backed save system, allowing players to record their extensive progress in an expansive open world. This feature redefined how adventure games were designed.
loadingScreen.description6: The name "Zelda" (from The Legend of Zelda franchise) was inspired by Zelda Fitzgerald—the wife of author F. Scott Fitzgerald—giving the series an exotic and memorable title.
loadingScreen.description7: The original Final Fantasy (1987), was conceived as developer Square's (later Square Enix) last-ditch effort during a financial crisis. Ironically, its unexpected success not only saved the company but also laid the groundwork for one of the most iconic and enduring RPG franchises.
